Subject: Budget anchor qualification + margin workbook — follow-up from demo

Hi Alyssa / Evan —

Great to meet you both today — thanks for making time. Quick recap and the asks so we can build a focused unit-econ workbook for your pilot.

What we covered (brief):
- Real-time summarization, triage routing, and auto-draft reply flows for inbound messages
- Expected latency / SLO constraints for triage path (sub-200ms for critical paths)
- Data residency & audit log requirements (noted your procurement items)

I need three quick inputs to populate the workbook and propose a tight pilot offer:
1) Token-volume signal: expected tokens/month for pilot (best guess range is fine). If you prefer, give MAU and avg tokens/session and I’ll compute.
2) Budget anchor: target monthly spend range you’re considering for the pilot (ballpark ok).
3) Business success criteria: minimum CAC payback horizon (months) and minimum gross margin target vs inference cost (e.g., target 50–60% gross margin).

If easier, reply with MAU / avg tokens per session / expected sessions per MAU and we’ll translate to $/1M token guidance.

Attachments: I uploaded the demo recording to the Drive link (see below). I’ll assemble a short unit-econ workbook and send back by tomorrow EOD.

Proposed next steps:
- You → quick volume + budget anchor reply (this thread) — by EOD today if possible.
- We → detailed workbook + recommended price bands — by Wed 6/30.
- 30m alignment call (procurement + engineering) — propose Thu 7/1 or Fri 7/2.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Vivek

Vivek — thanks for the recap and for the demo today. High level numbers from our side (pilot assumptions):

- Pilot cohort size: ~10k end users (narrow clinical beta across two clinics)
- Usage per active user: ~2 sessions/week average, ~600 tokens per session average -> ~4.8M tokens/month (range 3.5M–6.5M)
- Budget anchor: ~$12k–$22k / month for the pilot (can stretch if unit economics make sense)
- Commercial targets: want CAC payback <= 6 months for any pricing we sign to a committed pilot; prefer gross margin >= 55% vs inference-only spend (we'll account for product/ops on our side)
- Priority features for MVP: Summaries (high), triage routing (medium), canned-reply suggestions (low).

Let me know if this level of granularity is enough. Evan is our procurement lead and will be on the call for contract/contracting questions.

Alyssa Tan
Head of Product, HealthBridge

Subject: Re: Budget anchor qualification + margin workbook — follow-up from demo

Looping through the numbers quickly (attaching the workbook). Below are the key assumptions and a couple of pricing bands to test with HealthBridge.

Assumptions (pilot baseline):
- Volume: 4.8M tokens / month (midpoint of HealthBridge range)
- Redwood inferred variable cost (GPU + infra amortized + ops) = $1,600 / 1M tokens (this includes batching / KV cache benefits at pilot scale).
- Fixed platform & support overhead (apportioned) = $800 / 1M tokens (at this commit level).
- Total unit cost = $2,400 / 1M tokens.

Target margin scenarios (gross margin vs total unit cost):
- 50% margin => price = $4,800 / 1M tokens
- 60% margin => price = $6,000 / 1M tokens
- 70% margin => price = $8,000 / 1M tokens

Recommended pilot price bands (for negotiation):
- Intro band (3 months, low friction): $3,200 / 1M tokens (loss-leading vs 60% target) with 3-month minimum and 4.8M tokens committed/mo.
- Mid band (recommended): $4,500 / 1M tokens with 3–6 month commit — this meets ~46% margin and gives room for extensions.
- Std band (for long-term): $6,000 / 1M tokens with 12-month commit — aligns with 60% margin target.

$/feature rough mapping (pilot):
- Summaries (per active user cost, assuming 2 summaries / session): ~ $0.12 / user / month at 4.8M tokens (high level)
- Triage routing (latency-critical): ~ $0.25 / user / month (because of lower batching efficiency)
- Canned replies: ~ $0.05 / user / month

CAC payback worked example (illustrative):
- If average CAC to acquire a pilot clinic = $2,400 and expected incremental ARR contribution per clinic = $12,000/year -> payback = ~2.4 months at mid-band pricing.
- If CAC = $6,000 and incremental ARR = $12,000 -> payback = 6 months (meets HealthBridge target).

Notes / recommendations:
- HealthBridge target margin >=55% implies list price closer to $5.5–6k / 1M tokens; offer intro band to land the pilot and follow up with a transition to mid/std band tied to usage milestones.
- We should model sensitivity to token efficiency (e.g., if average tokens/session goes up 20%, unit cost drops ~8–10% due to batching).

Attachments: redwood_unit_econ_workbook_v1.xlsx (contains per-feature tabs, sensitivity graphs, and a CAC-payback calculator).

Ben Carter
Head of Product Economics | Redwood Inference
